title: Sarma Names Four Ministers for Assam's New Cabinet
excerpt: Rameswar Teli, Atul Bora, Charan Boro, and Ajanta Neog to take oath alongside CM on May 12 in Guwahati
body:
Himanta Biswa Sarma, set to be sworn in as Assam Chief Minister for a second consecutive term, named four ministers who will join him at the oath-taking ceremony on Tuesday, May 12, in Guwahati — with Prime Minister Narendra Modi present.

**The four ministers named:**
Sarma announced via X that former Union Minister Rameswar Teli, Asom Gana Parishad president Atul Bora, United People's Party Liberal leader Charan Boro, and senior BJP leader Ajanta Neog will join him at the ceremony. Sarma wrote that all four colleagues will 'take oath as Ministers tomorrow along with me in the august presence of Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji.' Senior BJP MLA Ranjit Das has been named the NDA's candidate for the post of Speaker of the Assam Legislative Assembly.

**A mandate built on a landslide:**
This swearing-in follows a sweeping electoral verdict. The BJP-led NDA won 102 of 126 assembly seats — BJP alone secured 82 — marking the first time since Independence that a single non-Congress party secured an outright majority in Assam. Congress managed only 19 seats, a sharp decline that underscores how decisively voters backed Sarma's governance record. Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal called it 'a great day for the people of Assam,' expressing confidence the state will 'become one of the most developed in the country.'

**What to watch:**
The initial cabinet of five is lean by design — portfolio allocation and a fuller cabinet expansion are expected in the days following the swearing-in ceremony.
nri_angle: Assam is home to one of India's largest Assamese and Bengali-origin diaspora communities in the U.S., and Sarma's third-term NDA government will shape policies on identity, citizenship, and the NRC — issues that directly touch families with roots in the region.
author: Diaspora Desk
